questions.q: $\mathrm{Pt}+3: 1$ mixture of (conc. $\mathrm{HCl}+$ conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ ) $\rightarrow[\mathrm{X}]^2$ What is the oxidation state of Pt in $[\mathrm{X}]^{2-}$ complex ion?
questions.solution:
When Pt reacts with a $3: 1$ mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid $(\mathrm{HCl})$ and concentrated nitric acid $\left(\mathrm{HNO}_3\right)$, It forms a solution known as aqua regia. aqua regia is capable of dissolving platinum by forming chlorocomplexes. The reaction typically forms $\mathrm{H}_2\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_6\right]$ In this complex. The $\mathbf{P t}$ is in the +4 oxidation state. The Balance chemical equation for the reaction is $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Pa}+4 \mathrm{HNO}_2+6 \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\left[\mathrm{Pt} \mathrm{Cl}_6\right]+4 \mathrm{NO}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ & \mathrm{Ht} \end{aligned}$
So $\operatorname{In} \mathrm{H}_2\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_6\right]$ the oxidation state of Pt $\begin{aligned} & =+2(x-6)=0 \\ & x-4=0 \\ & x=+4 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Identify the pair of reactions undergoing disproportionation from the following.
questions.solution:
Disproportionation Reaction: -
Reaction in which an element is oxidised as well as reduced.

(1) Cl20+OH-→Cl--1+Cl+1O-+H2O
Since, there is both decrease and increase of oxidation states of chlorine, chlorine is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction. Therefore, it is a disproportionation reaction.

(2) 2H2O2-1→2H2O-2+O20
Since, there is both decrease and increase in the O.N. of oxygen, H2O2 is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction. Therefore, it is a disproportionation reaction.

The oxidation state of $\mathrm{Pb}$ in each species is +2 and +4 respectively.
In $\mathrm{PbO} \rightarrow x+(-2)=0\begin{aligned}
x & =+2 \\
\mathrm{PbO}_2 \rightarrow x+2 \times(-2) & =0 \\
x-4 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x & =+4
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not a disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
In disproportionation reaction, oxidation state of one compound convert to the two compounds, one of higher and one of lower oxidation state.
In both the compounds, $\mathrm{F}^{-}$and $\mathrm{OF}_2$, oxidation state of $\mathrm{F}$ is -1 . Hence, fluorine does not disproportionate. Oxygen also has -2 oxidation state, but in product its oxidation state becomes +2 in $\mathrm{OF}_2$ but still is -2 in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

KMnO4 oxidises oxalic acid in acidic medium to carbon dioxide. The balanced equation can be represented as follows,

According to the above balanced equation, 2 moles of potassium permanganate produces the 10 moles of carbon dioxide. The number of CO2 molecules produced per mole of KMnO4 is 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
From the given reactions identify the disproportionation reaction
i) Cl2(g)+2KI(aq)⟶2KCl(aq)+I2(s)
ii) Cl2(g)+2OH-(aq)⟶ClO-(aq)+Cl-(aq)+H2O(l)
iii) Mg(s)+2HCl(aq)⟶MgCl2(aq)+H2(g)
iv) 2H2O2(aq)⟶2H2O(l)+O2(g)
questions.solution:
The reaction in which one reactant gets oxidized, and the same reactant gets reduced is known as disproportionation reaction. 

Cl02(g)+2KI-1(aq)⟶2KC0l(aq)+I-12(s)

In the above reaction different elements undergoing oxidation and reduction. Hence, It is not a disproportionation reaction. 

Cl02(g)+2OH-(aq)⟶Cl+1O-(aq)+Cl-(aq)+H2O(l)

In the above reaction chlorine is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction. Hence, It is a disproportionation reaction. 

Mg0(s)+2H+1Cl(aq)⟶Mg+2Cl2(aq)+H02(g)

In the above reaction magnesium is undergoing oxidation and hydrogen ion undergoing reduction. Hence, It is not a disproportionation reaction. 

2H2O-12(aq)⟶2H2O-2(l)+O02(g)

In the above reaction peroxide is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction. Hence, It is a disproportionation reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the titration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mfenced><mi>aq</mi></mfenced></math> by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>aq</mi></mfenced></math> using the starch indicator, the end point is indicated by:
questions.solution:
Titration of iodine (I2) by thiosulphate solution (S2O32-) follows the reaction:

2S2O32-+I2→2I-+S4O62-

In the presence of starch, free iodine present in the solution imparts blue colour to the solution.

End point marks the completion of reaction, that is, at this point all the iodine present in the solution is reduced to iodide ions by thiosulphate solution.

So, due to the absence of free iodine in the solution, the solution turns colourless.

Thus, the end point is indicated by colour change in the solution from blue to colourless.

3 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{2-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{MnO}_2+2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}+4 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \\
x=3, y=2, p=1 ; q=2 ; r=4
\end{gathered}$
Thus, option (4) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the oxidation states of $\mathrm{Mn}$, when $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{2-}$ ion undergoes disproportionation reaction under acidic medíum.
questions.solution:
The disproportionation reaction for $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{2-}$ occurs as follows :
$3 \stackrel{+6}{\mathrm{MnO}_4^{2-}}+4 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow \stackrel{+4}{\mathrm{MnO}_2}+2 \stackrel{+7}{\mathrm{M} n} \mathrm{MO}_4^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
Hence, $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{2-}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$and reduced to $\mathrm{MnO}_2$. Thus, oxidation state of $\mathrm{Mn}$ when $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{2-}$ undergoes disproportionation reaction under acidic medium are +7 and +4 .
$\therefore$ Hence option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the following:
The correct answer is $\begin{array}{llllllll}A & B & C & D & A & B & C & D\end{array}$
questions.solution:
(A) $\mathrm{TiCl}_4(l)+2 \mathrm{Mg}(s) \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Ti}(s)+2 \mathrm{MgCl}_2(s)$
The above reaction is an example of metal displacement reaction in which more reactive metal. (i.e. $\mathrm{Mg}$ ) will displace less reactive metal (i.e. Ti).
Thus, option (II) is related with (A).
(B) $2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2(a q) \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$
The above reaction is an example of disproportionation reaction in which $\mathrm{O}$-atom of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ is oxidised as $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$ and also reduced to $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. Thus, option (I) is related with (B).
(C) $\mathrm{C}(s)+\mathrm{O}_2(g) \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CO}_2(g)$
The above reaction is an example of combination reaction in which carbon(s) combines with $\mathrm{O}_2(g)$ to give $\mathrm{CO}_2(g)$. Thus, option (IV) is related with (C).
(D) $2 \mathrm{NaH}(s) \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{Na}(s)+\mathrm{H}_2(g)$
The above reaction is an example of decomposition reaction in which $\mathrm{NaH}$ is decomposes to $\mathrm{Na}(s)$ and $\mathrm{H}_2(g)$. Thus, option (III) is related with (D).
Hence,
$(\mathrm{A}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{II}),(\mathrm{B}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{I}),(\mathrm{C}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{IV}),(\mathrm{D}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{III})$
and option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $25 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.1 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{NaOH}$ solution neutralises $12.5 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $\mathrm{HCl}$ solution. The amount of water needed to convert $500 \mathrm{~mL}$ of such $\mathrm{HCl}$ solution to $0.1 \mathrm{~N}$ is
questions.solution:
$\because$ Concentration of $\mathrm{NaOH}\left(N_1\right)=0.1 \mathrm{~N}$
Volume of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ used $\left(V_1\right)=25 \mathrm{~mL}$
Concentration of $\mathrm{HCl}\left(N_2\right)=0.1 \mathrm{~N}$
Volume of $\mathrm{HCl}\left(V_2\right)$ used $=V_2$
and
$N_1 V_1=N_2 V_2$
Thus,
$V_2=\frac{N_1 V_1}{N_2}=\frac{0.1 \times 25}{0.1}$
Volume of $\mathrm{HCl}$ used $\left(V_2\right)=25 \mathrm{~mL}=V_1$
Thus, to convert $500 \mathrm{~mL} \mathrm{HCl}$ solution to $0.1 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{HCl}$, we need $500 \mathrm{~mL}$ of water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The following reaction occurs in acidic medium
$\mathrm{KMnO}_4+8 \mathrm{H}^{+}+5 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}^{+}+\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
What is the equivalent weight of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ ?
(Molecular weight of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4=158$)
questions.solution:
In the reaction (in acidic medium),
$\mathrm{KMnO}_4+8 \mathrm{H}^{+}+5 \mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}^{+}+\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium. $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ gains 5 electrons from reductant.
$\therefore$ Equivalent weight of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4=\frac{158}{5}=31.6 \text { (in g/equivalent) }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One third litre of $x \mathrm{MK}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$ is required to completely oxidise $2 \mathrm{~L}$ of $0.1 \mathrm{M}$ ferrous ammonium sulphate in acid medium. What Is $x$ ?
questions.solution:
$x M \mathrm{~K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+6 \mathrm{FeSO}_4+7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \longrightarrow 7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{Cr}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3+3 \mathrm{Fe}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3+\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4\mathrm{FeSO} \cdot 4 \cdot\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot 6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \text { is Mohr salt }(0.1 \mathrm{M})$
Given, $V_1$ (volume of $\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$ ) $=\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~L}$
Here, $\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$ is required to completely oxidise ferrous ammonium sulphate $(0.1 \mathrm{M})$. Therefore, molarity of $\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7=0.1 \mathrm{M}$
Thus, option (2) is correct.
